rules.title: Agreement enquiry: the two parties

source_locator.passage_anchor: The Lord of the Ascendant is for him that asks
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.title: Alternative testimonies of concord

source_locator.passage_anchor: If a benevolent Planet be in the third
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

any_of: third lord is a benevolent planet
third lord and Ascendant lord in sextile or trine within the orbs of either planet
mutual reception of third lord and Ascendant lord
third lord casts sextile or trine to Ascendant cusp
Ascendant lord casts sextile or trine to third house
source_statement.outcome: unity and concord between the querent and the specified brother, sister, neighbour or kinsman

qualifications_and_limits: Alternatives are not all-required. The explicit orb qualification belongs to the two-lord planetary aspect branch; no new numerical orb or global conflict-resolution rule is supplied.

rules.title: Asymmetric contact and attribution of the defect

source_locator.passage_anchor: if a Fortune be in the Ascendant or the Lord of the Ascendant behold the cusp of the third
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: A Fortune in Ascendant or Ascendant lord beholding third cusp, together with third lord not aspecting either Ascendant or its lord, attributes good condition/no default to querent and the defect to the other party.
qualifications_and_limits: The source's compound punctuation is not a formal Boolean expression; the natural conjunction with absent reciprocal contact is preserved. Behold is not narrowed to a favourable aspect. This is historical fault attribution, not an established fact about actual people.

rules.title: Ascendant malefics and fault

source_locator.passage_anchor: Saturn, Mars or South Node in the Ascendant
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Saturn, Mars or South Node in Ascendant is assigned to fault or ill condition of the querent.
qualifications_and_limits: No essential-dignity exception is stated for this Ascendant clause. Historical characterization only.

rules.title: Third-house adverse bodies and dignity exception

source_locator.passage_anchor: if they be in the third, unlesse in their own essentiall dignities
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Saturn, Mars or South Node in third gives little good from the other party unless in own essential dignities; worse if peregrine, retrograde, combust or in any malevolent configuration with another planet.
qualifications_and_limits: Worsening predicates are alternatives. The node's inclusion in the dignity-qualified phrase does not supply it an invented domicile or dignity table.

rules.title: Present concord can fail later

source_locator.passage_anchor: although at present there be unity
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: In the preceding adverse third-house configuration, apparent present unity does not promise continuation; Lilly says hatred or grumbling usually follows.
prerequisites: The preceding adverse third-house context applies.
qualifications_and_limits: Usually is retained; no deterministic date or categorical universal.
rules.temporal_target: Present unity versus later continuation; no duration

rules.title: Saturn or South Node character attribution

source_locator.passage_anchor: Saturn or South Node in the third
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Saturn or South Node in third characterizes neighbours as clowns and kin as covetous or sparing, most assuredly out of essential dignities.
qualifications_and_limits: Historical moral attribution, not an observed personal trait. Source dignity language is retained without inventing node dignities.

rules.title: Mars character attribution

source_locator.passage_anchor: Mars, then your Kindred are treacherous
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Mars in third characterizes kin as treacherous and neighbours as thievish, most assuredly when out of essential dignities.
qualifications_and_limits: Historical moral attribution, not an observed personal trait.

rules.title: Absent brother: house frame

source_locator.passage_anchor: Of a Brother that is absent
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

source_statement.continuation: proceed in order through the other houses

qualifications_and_limits: The following house numbers are preserved as the source writes them. Read with the explicit original-figure sixth/eighth/twelfth qualification on PDF226 and the dual-eighth worked example on PDF231.

rules.title: Inspect the brother's significator and contacts

source_locator.passage_anchor: consider the Lord of the third, in what condition he is
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

source_statement: aspect from good or evil planets

rules.title: Third lord in third without malefic square or opposition

source_locator.passage_anchor: If the Lord of the third be in the third
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Third lord in third with no square or opposition from unfortunate planets signifies the brother in health.
qualifications_and_limits: The glyph after square is opposition in the original; not conjunction.

rules.title: Third-house malefic contact without reception: distress while healthy

source_locator.passage_anchor: malignant Planets have a square or opposition unto him, without reception
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Malignant planets square or opposite the significator without reception signify that he lives and is in health, but in great perplexity, discontent and sorrow.
prerequisites: Retain the opening third-house placement/aspect-reading context before the text moves to fourth.
qualifications_and_limits: Distress is not silently recoded as illness. No direction or mutuality of reception is supplied.

rules.title: Third-house malefic contact with reception: escape from distress

source_locator.passage_anchor: if the same Infortunes have reception with him
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: The same malignant square/opposition with reception signifies great distress which he will evade with ease, freeing himself from the present sad condition.
prerequisites: Opening third-house context and the preceding malignant-contact branch.
qualifications_and_limits: Reception does not erase the distress premise. Direction and mutuality unspecified.
rules.temporal_target: Present distress and subsequent escape; no duration

rules.title: Benefic alternatives for health and contentment

source_locator.passage_anchor: fortunate Planets be in sextile or trine with him, without reception
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Fortunate planets sextile/trine the significator without reception, OR square/opposite him with reception, signify health and contentment to remain where he is.
qualifications_and_limits: The aspect/reception pairings are not interchangeable; not a generic any-benefic-contact rule.

rules.title: Benefic soft aspect with reception: stronger well-being claim

source_locator.passage_anchor: sextile or trine with him, and with reception
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Fortunate planets sextile/trine the significator with reception signify health and lack of nothing needed for happiness.
qualifications_and_limits: Stronger historical claim than mere contentment; no measured probability.

rules.title: Fourth placement and effort to obtain substance

source_locator.passage_anchor: If the Lord of the third be in the fourth
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Third lord in fourth, explicitly the brother's own second, without aspect of malignant planets signifies endeavour to obtain estate or fortune in the country where he is when the figure is erected.
qualifications_and_limits: Endeavour is not completed acquisition. Without aspect is not narrowed to square/opposition.

rules.title: Fifth placement with its lord

source_locator.passage_anchor: If he be in the fifth, and joyned with the Lord of the fifth
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Third lord in fifth, joined with fifth lord, 'with reception of a Fortune or not', provided fifth lord is not grievously impedited, signifies health, merriment and pleasure in the local company.
qualifications_and_limits: The unusual reception-of-a-Fortune wording is retained. It does not unambiguously identify fifth lord as a Fortune or require reception.

rules.title: Fifth-placement benefic mitigation and confidence

source_locator.passage_anchor: if the Lord of the fifth be a Fortune
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: In the local fifth-house discussion, a Fortune as the body with which the significator is conjunct, or a sextile/trine with reception, permits the favourable condition to be said more safely.
prerequisites: Fifth-placement context and the preceding qualification on the fifth lord.
qualifications_and_limits: The punctuation does not settle whether reception qualifies the conjunction as well as the sextile/trine alternative. No mutuality or confidence scale is invented.

rules.title: Fifth-placement void course or impedited malefic conjunction

source_locator.passage_anchor: if the Lord of the third be in the fifth, voyd of course
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Third lord in fifth void of course, OR in perfect conjunction with an unfortunate planet without reception and that planet itself impedited, argues indisposition in health, 'crazy', and discontent with the place.
qualifications_and_limits: Keep the fifth-house context and the two alternatives. Crazy is an archaic source word, not an established modern psychiatric diagnosis.

rules.title: Obscured qualification of naturally ill houses

source_locator.passage_anchor: other houses which are [cancelled word] naturally ill
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: A following statement places the significator in other houses 'which are [obscured/cancelled word] naturally ill (as the sixth, eighth and twelfth houses are)' and says he is not well pleased, yet no hurt will come of it.
qualifications_and_limits: The inked word could materially change the condition. Neither restoring 'not' nor deleting it is admitted as a clean source condition.

rules.title: Eighth placement with a Fortune: qualified indisposition

source_locator.passage_anchor: If the Significator be in the eighth, and corporally joyned to a Fortune
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Significator in eighth, corporally joined or joined by sextile/trine to a Fortune, is not very well but not so ill as to doubt well-being; still indisposed.
qualifications_and_limits: Reception is not stated as a requirement in this clause. Retain eighth placement for each contact alternative.

rules.title: Affliction out of the sixth

source_locator.passage_anchor: joyned to evill Planets by bad aspects, and out of the sixt house
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Joining evil planets by bad aspects 'and out of the sixth house' signifies infirmity.
qualifications_and_limits: Out of is not translated as outside the sixth. Its attachment to the afflicting body or aspect origin remains unresolved; no geometry is silently supplied.

rules.title: Sixth lord in third: dignity exception

source_locator.passage_anchor: if the Lord of the sixth be in the third
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Sixth lord in third gives the same infirmity judgement unless that lord has dignities in the sign and is in those dignities.
qualifications_and_limits: The exception requires possession and occupation of the relevant dignities. Radical/turned source context remains explicit.

rules.title: Mortality claim requires an already ill brother

source_locator.passage_anchor: if you find the Brother is ill
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: If the brother has already been found ill, third lord conjunct eighth lord OR entering combustion makes it likely, in Lilly's judgement, that he will die of that infirmity.
prerequisites: Prior illness judgement; do not infer illness from this conditional alone.
qualifications_and_limits: Historical source claim, not an actual-person medical judgement; likely is not certainty.
rules.temporal_target: Likely future death from the specified existing illness; no date

rules.title: Seventh placement: continued sojourn

source_locator.passage_anchor: If the Significator be in the seventh
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Significator in seventh signifies remaining in the country to which he went, a stranger/sojourner, neither well nor ill.
qualifications_and_limits: A cancelled short word before went is not reconstructed; it supplies no extra destination or date.

rules.title: Eighth placement: fear of death

source_locator.passage_anchor: If he be in the eighth, he feares he shall dye
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Significator in eighth signifies his fear that he will die; greater fear if combust, OR conjunct eighth lord in eighth, OR square/opposite the Infortunes 'out of the eighth'.
qualifications_and_limits: Fear is the outcome here, not death. Preserve the eighth context and old aspect-origin phrase.

rules.title: Ninth placement: alternative places and employments

source_locator.passage_anchor: If he be in the ninth
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Significator in ninth signifies a further country; OR, if capable, entry into a religious order; OR employment by religious men; OR possibly a journey far from the former abode according to his quality.
qualifications_and_limits: Alternatives and personal capacity/status qualifiers remain; no single automatic occupation or location.

rules.title: Tenth placement with Fortunes

source_locator.passage_anchor: If he be in the tenth, and joyned with Fortunes
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Significator in tenth conjunct or sextile/trine Fortunes, especially with reception, signifies office, employment or command, good estimation and credible living in that country.
qualifications_and_limits: Reception strengthens rather than exclusively gates the stated good contact alternatives.

rules.title: Adverse tenth placement: feared death

source_locator.passage_anchor: joyned to Infortunes, or in square or opposition
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: In tenth, joining Infortunes, square/opposing them, being otherwise impedited by them, OR combustion leads Lilly to say it may be feared he is dead.
qualifications_and_limits: Do not equate may be feared with a confirmed death, the absent person's own fear, or the preceding likely future death conditional.
rules.temporal_target: Tentative concern that death has already occurred

rules.title: Eleventh placement: friends and safety

source_locator.passage_anchor: If he be in the eleventh house
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Significator in eleventh joined to Fortunes by a good aspect, OR conjunct eleventh lord, signifies safety at a friend's house, pleasant and merry.
qualifications_and_limits: Eleventh placement applies to the surrounding alternatives.

rules.title: Afflicted eleventh placement

source_locator.passage_anchor: if evill Planets afflict him in that house
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Bad planets afflicting the significator in eleventh or casting malevolent beams to him signify discontent with his present condition.

rules.title: Twelfth placement with received unimpeded Fortunes

source_locator.passage_anchor: joyned to Fortunes with reception, and those Fortunes not impedited
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Significator in twelfth joined to Fortunes with reception, those Fortunes unimpeded, signifies dealings with horses or great cattle: grazier, master of horse, hostler, drover and similar alternatives according to his quality.
qualifications_and_limits: Reception, unimpeded Fortunes, placement and personal-quality qualifications are all retained; not every occupation simultaneously.

rules.title: Adverse twelfth placement: discontent, fear and probable death there

source_locator.passage_anchor: unfortunate in the twelfth, or in bad aspect with the infortunes
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: In the twelfth-house paragraph, being unfortunate, in bad aspect with Infortunes, in aspect with eighth lord, OR combust signifies discontent, fear of never seeing home again, and a probable death there.
prerequisites: Twelfth-house paragraph context; not an any-house combustion rule.
qualifications_and_limits: Eighth-lord aspect is not narrowed to bad aspect. Fear, discontent and author's qualified death claim remain separate endpoints.

rules.title: First placement: pleasure and respect

source_locator.passage_anchor: If he be in the first
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Significator in first signifies pleasure where he is and being loved and respected there.

rules.title: Second placement: probable impediment to leaving

source_locator.passage_anchor: If he be in the second
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Significator in second signifies probable inability to come away: imprisonment or an act preventing departure.
qualifications_and_limits: Alternative causes; probable is not certain imprisonment.

rules.title: Retrograde second-placement significator: effort to escape

source_locator.passage_anchor: if he be Retrograde
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: With the preceding impediment to leaving, retrogradation signifies strenuous effort to escape when opportunity appears.
qualifications_and_limits: Effort and opportunity do not guarantee successful escape.

rules.title: Absent father and extension round the houses

source_locator.passage_anchor: the fourth house is the Ascendant of that party
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: For an absent father, use fourth as his Ascendant and proceed round twelve houses. The paragraph calls the second house from 'the Ascendant of your Question' the quesited's substance, the third from that his brethren and the fourth his father.
qualifications_and_limits: The quoted reference phrase is awkward beside the explicit derived Ascendant. Preserve it; the later child/servant examples make inclusive turning explicit without erasing the wording ambiguity.

rules.title: Absent child frame

source_locator.passage_anchor: if one aske of his childe, son or daughter
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.title: Absent servant frame

source_locator.passage_anchor: If one aske of a Servant
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.title: Original figure sixth, eighth and twelfth retained

source_locator.passage_anchor: yet in every one quesited after, the sixt House of the figure
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Although every house has its own sixth, eighth and twelfth, Lilly explicitly retains sixth of the figure for the absent person's infirmity, eighth for death and twelfth for imprisonment.
qualifications_and_limits: This statement coexists with the turning instructions and the worked dual-eighth check on PDF231. It neither deletes derived houses nor supplies a universal numerical precedence rule.

rules.title: Variation is required but not formalized

source_locator.passage_anchor: you must know how to vary your Rules
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Lilly calls varying the rules the masterpiece of the art and expects a judicious practitioner to do so.
qualifications_and_limits: No new discretion score, tie-breaker, or retrospective permission to choose whichever interpretation fits is implemented.

rules.title: Alternative ancient frames for intelligence

source_locator.passage_anchor: The Ancients placed these judgments variously
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Some Ancients use fifth; others use triplicity lords of signs ascending/descending on third or fifth cusps for reports, news, intelligence and fears.
qualifications_and_limits: The text reports alternatives rather than choosing a single fully specified algorithm.

rules.title: Lilly's wartime report truth and parliamentary benefit

source_locator.passage_anchor: I have ever found by experience
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_attribution: Lilly's declared late Civil War experience
rules.source_statement: Moon in first, tenth, eleventh or third, separated by a benevolent aspect from any planet regardless of its house lordship, then applying by sextile, trine or conjunction to Ascendant lord, is reported by Lilly as true news which always tended to Parliament's good, whether the report sounded good or ill.
qualifications_and_limits: Placement, separation, application and recipient are conjunctive conditions; three application types are visible in the original. Truth, tone and beneficiary are distinct. The historical partisan claim is not a generic prediction of querent victory.

rules.title: Lilly's wartime enemy-benefit alternative

source_locator.passage_anchor: if the Moon applyed to the Lord of the seventh
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Moon applying to seventh lord by any good aspect at figure erection made Lilly judge his side had the worst and the enemies the victory.
qualifications_and_limits: Does not by itself state that the report is false; political benefit and report truth are different targets.

rules.title: Void-of-course Moon and inconsequential reports

source_locator.passage_anchor: Moon was voyd of course
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Void-of-course Moon made Lilly judge news of no moment, usually vain or mere lies and soon contradicted.
qualifications_and_limits: Usually is retained. Inconsequence and falsity are not equivalent outcomes.
rules.temporal_target: Near-term contradiction claimed; no fixed interval

rules.title: Moon-Mercury hard aspect plus absent favourable Ascendant contact

source_locator.passage_anchor: Moon and Mercury in square or opposition
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Moon and Mercury square/opposite, with neither or both supplying any favourable sextile/trine to the Ascendant degree, is interpreted as false news deliberately reported to frighten Lilly's side.
qualifications_and_limits: Meaning: neither body supplies such a favourable contact; it is not merely that both fail to do so jointly. The degree target and missing-favourable-contact condition are necessary.

rules.title: News question time depends on who asks

source_locator.passage_anchor: the houre when I first heard the newes
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

source_statement.self_heard_news: moment of first hearing the news or rumour
source_statement.another_person_proposes_question: exact moment the question is proposed

qualifications_and_limits: Historical procedural convention, not a modern message-delivery or automated-interview rule.

rules.title: Whether news harms the asker: favourable alternatives

source_locator.passage_anchor: see whether Jupiter or Venus be in the Ascendant
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Jupiter or Venus in Ascendant, OR Moon or Mercury in their essential dignities with trine/sextile to eleventh lord, signifies no detriment to the person enquiring.
prerequisites: The enquiry is whether the report will be prejudicial to the asker.
qualifications_and_limits: Original first pair is Jupiter/Venus, not Moon/Mercury. Dignity-plus-aspect belongs to the Moon/Mercury branch; no-detriment is not necessarily report falsity.

rules.title: Harm from news: relevance and planetary conditions

source_locator.passage_anchor: Lord of the sixth, eighth or twelfth houses in the Ascendant
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Sixth, eighth or twelfth lord in Ascendant or in bad aspect to Ascendant lord; OR Mars/Saturn retrograde in Ascendant, in evil aspect to Ascendant lord, or casting square/opposition to Ascendant degree, signifies harm to querent if the matter concerns that person, or damage to ministers/parties if it concerns the Commonwealth.
qualifications_and_limits: Relevance and target are required. The reach of retrograde into the later Mars/Saturn alternatives is less than formally explicit; preserve its printed position.

rules.title: Wartime damage examples by actual significator

source_locator.passage_anchor: if Saturn signifie the mischiefe
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

source_statement.Saturn: country friends plundered; corn and cattle lost
source_statement.Sun: chief officer or commander in distress
source_statement.Jupiter_or_Venus: harm to gentlemen, friends or supporters

prerequisites: The harm/Commonwealth context applies and the named planet actually signifies the mischief.
qualifications_and_limits: Not a claim about every occurrence of these planets; Lilly explicitly says to vary by the question.

rules.title: Ancients' angularity, fixity and favourable-contact alternatives

source_locator.passage_anchor: Consider the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Consider Ascendant lord and Moon and which is angular; OR Moon's dispositor angular and fixed; OR any of these succedent and fixed; OR in sextile/trine to Jupiter, Venus or Sun: the rumours are judged true and very good.
qualifications_and_limits: The reach of fixed sign across the opening angular alternatives is not formally unambiguous. Sun is explicitly in the favourable list.

rules.title: Afflicted or cadent first lord overrides own-sign strength here

source_locator.passage_anchor: if you find the Lord of the Ascendant afflicted
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Ascendant lord afflicted by Infortunes OR cadent gives the contrary judgement, though strong in its sign.
qualifications_and_limits: Do not erase the contrary clause by selecting sign strength alone.

rules.title: Fixed angles and applying Moon/Mercury

source_locator.passage_anchor: Rumours are for the most part true
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Rumours are for the most part true with fixed angles (Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius), Moon and Mercury in fixed signs separating from Infortunes and applying to a fortunate planet in an angle.
qualifications_and_limits: All configuration components, including the angular recipient and movement sequence, are retained; for the most part is not certainty.

rules.title: Ill report partly verified with fixed fourth/tenth

source_locator.passage_anchor: Ill Rumours hold true
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: Ill rumours with fourth and tenth angles fixed and Moon 'received in them' will in some sort be verified.
qualifications_and_limits: In some sort does not certify every detail. Received in them is not a fully defined mutual-reception or placement formula.

rules.title: Ill news turns good: Fortune branch and uncertain Moon word

source_locator.passage_anchor: if either of the Fortunes be in the Ascendant, or the Moon ufortunate
source_locator.anchor_note: Locating incipit/topic; long-s, spacing and glyph names normalized. Not a diplomatic quotation.

rules.source_statement: For evil news or unlucky intelligence, either Fortune in Ascendant OR Moon described by the visibly printed 'ufortunate' is called strong evidence that rumours are false and will turn to good.
